evidence_quotes.quote: On the other hand, although households receive water from a piped water supply system, it is not considered to be well maintained or to provide a constant supply (low risk) in accordance with the indicators as defined above in Table 1.

In place of the microbial indices used in detailed QMRA-based studies, a set of proxy indicators is used as the basis for the quantification of risk. In the methodology, factors that define the physical, environmental and social conditions along with individual susceptibility to disease are all treated as important predictors of illness in a community.
The approach is intended for local authorities, environmental health officers, and utility/service providers to better understand the existing risks in the sanitation chain.

It consisted of a detailed questionnaire that expanded upon the indicators used for the RPSSRA in the community workshop. Each household survey took approximately 20 minutes to complete. A total of 160 surveys were undertaken using a random sampling method that started at a selected point in the area.

The methodology described in this paper utilizes local stakeholder knowledge in a participatory process to score sanitation risks, using a framework of indicators that provides a quantitative assessment of the intensity and distribution of risk.

criterion_notes.c1: Examines urban household and community sanitation and water service conditions in two low-income neighbourhoods of Maputo (Chamanculo C and Chamanculo D), including toilet coverage, pit-latrine desludging services, shared latrines, wastewater disposal, solid waste collection, and piped water supply reliability as components of a sanitary risk index.
criterion_notes.c2: Fails both the plain wording and the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading of Criterion 2. Under the plain wording, the study does not empirically examine any legal, administrative, institutional, regulatory, or governance factor: local administration and a partner NGO only assisted logistically with sub-area boundary definition and workshop participant selection, and city sanitation planning by local authorities or utilities is discussed solely as a prospective application of the risk-mapping tool rather than an analysed variable. Under the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading, no rule-type mechanism directly governing service access (such as eligibility screening, administrative burden, documentation or tenure requirements, tariff or cost-recovery rules, discretion or accommodation, enforcement, or utility ownership/regulatory structure) is studied.
criterion_notes.c3: Contains primary empirical data from participatory community risk-scoring workshops (20–25 participants per neighbourhood in Chamanculo C and Chamanculo D) and a random-sample validation survey of 160 households in Chamanculo C.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports indicator-level risk scores (0–100% rescaled from 1–3 traffic-light categories) that summarize community-level toilet coverage, desludging service adequacy, latrine sharing, and piped water supply reliability/maintenance alongside composite sanitary health risk scores.
criterion_notes.c5: Population, unit of analysis (sub-neighbourhood areas and surveyed households), methodological comparison/indicators, and risk-score outcomes are clearly described within a mixed participatory workshop and cross-sectional household validation survey design, though a legal/governance exposure is absent.

study_design: Participatory community risk assessment (workshops) validated against a cross-sectional random-sample household sanitary survey
population_and_sample: Residents of two low-income high-density neighbourhoods in Maputo (Chamanculo C, pop. 38,696, and Chamanculo D, pop. 20,236), divided into four sub-areas each; 20–25 workshop participants per neighbourhood and 160 randomly sampled households surveyed in Chamanculo C
exposure: Assessment modality (participatory community workshop scoring via RPSSRA vs. household sanitary survey) and physical, environmental, behavioural, and demographic sanitary risk indicators; no legal, administrative, regulatory, or governance factor examined
outcome: Indicator-specific and aggregate sanitary risk scores (0–100%) covering toilet coverage, toilet condition, desludging, wastewater disposal, solid waste, stormwater drainage, settlement density, latrine sharing, water supply, hygiene behaviour, housing condition, children per family, and education, plus percentage divergence between workshop and survey scores
rationale: Excluded under E03 (Wrong exposure). This empirical study develops and validates the Rapid Participatory Sanitation System Risk Assessment (RPSSRA) methodology in two low-income neighbourhoods of Maputo by comparing participatory workshop risk scores against a 160-household sanitary survey across 14 physical, environmental, behavioural, and socio-demographic indicators. It fails Criterion 2 under both the plain wording and the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading because it does not examine any legal, administrative, institutional, regulatory, or governance factor or rule-type mechanism governing water or sanitation service access; municipal planning is mentioned only as an intended downstream use of the risk-mapping tool.
